issues: Dolphin is rendered as a stippled dot/particle cloud instead of a continuous lit-phosphor silhouette, so it reads as starfield noise rather than a glowing creature.
A rectangular scatter-dot field (de-facto bounding box) surrounds the dolphin, adding clutter that does not exist on a real Pioneer OEL panel.
Dolphin edges are eroded by the dot texture; dorsal fin, tail fluke and pectoral fin lack the crisp rim light the reference calls for.
Dolphin has almost no phosphor bloom/halo, so it fails the 'lit phosphor object' requirement and looks flat/dotted.
No visible persistence/afterglow trail, so the leaping motion reads as a frozen static frame.
Top-left track text ('DJ BOBO / EVERYBODY') is high-contrast and bright enough to compete with the dolphin for first glance.
Extra telemetry readouts on the bottom-right (92BPM 8A, PHR 11/32, MIX 0:00 AT 02) are not part of the reference layout and add visual noise.
VU blocks in the bottom-left are comparatively bright, slightly pulling the eye away from the center.
suggestions: Replace the particle/stipple dolphin with a filled or cleanly outlined lit-phosphor silhouette so the body, dorsal fin, tail fluke and pectoral fin form one solid glowing shape.
Delete the rectangular scatter-dot field around the dolphin and keep the surrounding area as clean dark phosphor with at most a faint ambient glow.
Add a subtle, tight bloom halo around the dolphin silhouette so it glows like an OEL object while keeping the core edges crisp (not blown out).
Add a thin rim-light highlight along the dolphin's back and tail edge to restore definition lost to the dot rendering.
Introduce a short, decaying persistence trail along the leap arc to convey motion without fogging the whole scene.
Dim the top-left track text one or two brightness steps so the dolphin unambiguously wins the visual hierarchy.
Remove or strongly dim the bottom-right telemetry text to match the reference composition.
Lower the VU-meter block brightness slightly and confirm the FFT bars and wave lines stay the dimmest layers on screen.
